Selected evidence

Teaching Philosophy

I teach through a problem-to-evidence-to-decision sequence. Participants first frame an authentic business question, compare relevant theories and evidence, challenge assumptions, assess alternatives and risks, and defend an actionable recommendation. Cases draw on entrepreneurship, B2B sales, agrifood enterprises, marketing management, and international commercial operations.

My classrooms combine concise conceptual input with live business cases, facilitated discussion, practical assignments, and explicit evaluation criteria. I distinguish verified facts, estimates, and working assumptions, and encourage learners to test proposed solutions against measurable outcomes. Digital learning resources and applied AI are used when they help participants reason more clearly, not as substitutes for academic judgment.

Professional Capabilities & Tools

Business and leadership: Entrepreneurship; business operations; business development; strategic marketing; international market-entry analysis; stakeholder and supplier management; retail/B2B commercial planning; product development.
Teaching and research: Higher-education facilitation; curriculum development; adult learning; case-based teaching; questionnaire design; marketing research; evidence appraisal; student assessment; instructional technology.
Applied digital and AI workflows: ChatGPT and other AI-assisted research tools; Google Sheets/Excel; reporting dashboards and Looker Studio; HubSpot CRM; workflow design and process documentation; marketing research and competitive-intelligence tools. Tool use varies by project and does not imply advanced software-engineering or statistical-programming certification.
